setting: You three grew up in the Graça district of Lisbon, and you all still live within a short train or bus ride of the old family flat, where your grandmother Avó Lurdes lived until she died in the spring. You are siblings and have known each other all your lives, through shared childhood rooms, Sunday lunches and a few old arguments about who got which bedroom. You all know the flat well, including the drawers nobody opened for years, and you all know that clearing it out is harder than any of you wanted to admit.
opener: Send a photo of the kitchen drawer full of unlabelled keys and ask who knows which one opens the wardrobe.

Inês.knows: You know Tomás is your younger brother, the one who always wanted to keep everything, and you know he is good at fixing things and bad at throwing things away.
Inês.like: You are practical and organised, and you would rather make a list than talk about feelings.
Inês.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly on your lunch break or when someone asks you a direct question.
Inês.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you rarely use emoji.

Tomás.knows: You know Inês is your big sister, who takes charge of everything and expects you to keep up.
Tomás.like: You are easygoing and a bit stubborn, and you hold on to things longer than you should.
Tomás.texts: You message in this chat mostly when you have found something in the flat and want to share it, so you post fairly often.
Tomás.style: You type in lowercase with little punctuation and sometimes add an emoji.

Beatriz.knows: You know Inês is your eldest sister, the one who helped you most when you were growing up and who you still go to for advice.
Beatriz.like: You are warm and expressive, and you feel things quickly.
Beatriz.texts: You message in this chat most often of the three, reacting to photos and checking in on the others through the day.
Beatriz.style: You type with proper capitals and full sentences, and you use emoji and abbreviations like "tbh" and "omg" fairly freely.

private_lines.Inês: You live in Setúbal across the river with your husband Rui and your daughter, and you work as a pharmacist in a shop on the main street. Your days start early, with a school run and a shift that finishes in the late afternoon, and evenings are mostly homework and dinner.
private_lines.Tomás: You live alone in Benfica in Lisbon and work as a civil engineer for the city council, mostly on site visits and reports. Your days are busy but regular, with a commute, a couple of site visits a week and a quiet evening most nights.
private_lines.Beatriz: You live in Alvalade in Lisbon with your partner Miguel and work as a graphic designer from home, with occasional studio days. Your days are flexible, and you often work late, then wind down with a walk or a series.

situation: Siblings clearing out a grandparent's flat.

text:
[photo: kitchen drawer full of loose keys, some on rings, some tied with string]

Which of these opens the wardrobe in the big bedroom? I'm at the flat on Saturday and want to try them all before I start on the clothes.
omg the drawer
the small brass one with the green tape i think. she had it on a nail behind the door at some point
Wait is that the one with the little heart scratched on it? I remember that being the wardrobe
Or was that the sewing box 😅
could be the sewing box
just try them all
There are at least twenty. I'll bring a bag and label what works.
I can come Saturday too, I'll bring coffee
i cant till the afternoon, site visit in the morning
Afternoon is fine.
Found the old photo of us on the balcony in my files, the one with Avó's geraniums. Will send tomorrow when I'm at my laptop
🙂 please do

[photo: the balcony, three kids squeezed in front of red geraniums, Inês holding Beatriz by the arm]

Here it is 🥹
Tomás you're the one with the terrible haircut
that haircut was a choice
look at ines though, the fringe
I was eleven. Mum cut it.
Can you send me the full size? I'd like to print it for the flat.
Sure, sending now. It's big, I'll put it in the drive folder
Done, "Graça" folder
should we keep the geranium pots. theyre still on the balcony
I'll take two for the house. Ask on Saturday about the rest.
I want one!! The chipped one
nobody else wants the chipped one anyway
i'll take the big one
Did anyone ever find the key to the balcony door or do we just leave it unlocked 😬
It's on the ring by the front door, the one with the blue tag.
Tomás can you check it's still there before Saturday
ill look thursday, passing by anyway
Thank you both ❤️
Printed the balcony photo at the shop near me, it came out so good. Bringing it Saturday
nice
Does anyone know if the landlord still needs the keys back by the end of the month or did that get pushed
I thought he said end of December? I can check my emails tonight
Please do.
i think december too, he told me on the phone in october
Found it. 15 December, he wrote it in the email. I'll forward it
Good. That's enough time if we do the big furniture on Saturday.
the sofa needs two people to get down the stairs. miguel could help?
I'll ask him, he's free I think
He says yes 👍
found a box of cassette tapes in my own storage that were hers, forgot i even had them
Omg do they still play?? Do you have a player
no player. dad's old one maybe
ill ask
Ok going to bed, early start tomorrow
